title: GDP-Wage Transmission: reproducible estimation of productivity-to-wage transmission

creators.name: Ribeiro, Diogo
creators.affiliation: Faculty of Media Arts and Design, Technical University of Porto

description:
A reproducible empirical research repository for studying how economic growth and labour productivity transmit into real wages, how quickly that transmission occurs, and whether the relationship changes over time. The primary country is Portugal, with cross-country robustness analysis.

The model stack progresses from accounting identities to increasingly flexible time-series models: an exact national-accounts decomposition, stationarity and cointegration diagnostics, distributed-lag growth regressions, an Engle-Granger error-correction model, an endogenous least-squares structural-break search, formal single-break inference by sup-F with a wild bootstrap, a state-space time-varying transmission elasticity, local projections, an asymmetric transmission regression, optional VECM impulse responses, cross-country estimates reported country by country before any pooled summary, and a dynamic panel whose estimand is the same cumulative multiplier as the country models, corrected for dynamic fixed-effects bias and given a moving-block bootstrap interval.

Break dates are estimated rather than assumed: the structural-break and state-space models do not hard-code historical dates, and historical events are used only after estimation to interpret estimated regimes. Where a sample is too short to support a flexible specification, the result says so rather than reporting a coefficient without that caveat.

Reproducibility is enforced by construction. Official OECD and Eurostat extracts are stored unchanged with their query URL, retrieval timestamp and SHA-256 digest; analytical panels are rebuilt from those frozen bytes; a schema audit refuses to let a series mix units or price bases; and a release manifest records the package, interpreter, numerical-library and configuration state behind every result.

Nothing here is causal. The transmission elasticity is an association between jointly determined series, and a located break says when a relationship changed, never why.
